The boundary n=2 is handled. Independent Apéry checks n=2..160 and gcd/gluing checks n=2..300 reproduce the formulas.

value.rationale: Primitive normalization is the canonical way to pose a Frobenius problem for three consecutive tetrahedral terms whose unnormalized gcd is nontrivial. The theorem solves the entire natural three-term family, supplies exact F and genus at every index and a six-periodic arithmetic decomposition, and distinguishes its invariant from the previously studied four-term family. It does not claim a new general gluing theorem.
